summary: Alexander Piatigorsky worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. Educated at Moscow State University, he studied under George de Roerich and Bidia Dandaron, later holding posts at the Russian Academy of Sciences, Moscow State University, Oxford, and SOAS.
Alexander Rogers worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at the East India Company College from ~1843 to 1845 and served in the Indian Civil Service from ~1845 to 1878.

Alexander Rödel is a scholar in religious studies and Indology. He pursued a Master of Science by Research at the University of Edinburgh under the supervision of Steven Sutcliffe and Jeanne Openshaw (attested 2008).

Alexander W. Macdonald was a scholar of Tibetology, history, and archaeology. He held posts at the Musée de l'Homme (attested 1972) and Paris Nanterre University, where he was a professor from ~1978 to 1993.

Alexander Wynne specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He completed his undergraduate studies at the University of Bristol under Paul Williams and Rupert Gethin, and earned his DPhil at the University of Oxford supervised by Richard Gombrich.

Alexander Yiannopoulos works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at Ka-Nying Shedrub Ling Monastery, under traditional teachers Sherab Sangpo and Khenpo Sherab Dorje, and under supervisor Karin Myers, among other teachers.

Alexander von Humboldt was an explorer and scholar in history and archaeology. He studied at Frankfurt (Oder), Göttingen under Christian Gottlob Heyne and Georg Christoph Lichtenberg, and TU Bergakademie Freiberg, later holding a post at the University of Jena.

Alexander von Rospatt specializes in Indology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen, studied at the University of London, and held professorial posts at the University of Leipzig and UC Berkeley.

Alexander von Staël-Holstein worked in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Indology. After earning his doctorate at Halle-Wittenberg under Richard Pischel, he held posts at Saint Petersburg State University, Peking University, and directed the Sino-Indian Institute.

Alexandra David-Néel worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at the Royal Conservatory of Brussels (~1888–1891) and learned under Philippe-Édouard Foucaux (~1888–1894) and Kazi Dawa Samdup (1912).
Alexandra van der Geer is a scholar in Indology, history, and archaeology. She studied under Leendert A. van Daalen, Henk Bodewitz, and Paul Sondaar.

Alexandre Langlois was an Indologist who studied under Antoine-Léonard Chézy. He held positions as an inspector at the Académie de Paris, taught at Lycée Charlemagne, and was a member of the Académie des Inscriptions et Belles-Lettres (~1835–1854).

Alexis Sanderson is an Indology, religious studies, and philosophy scholar. He studied at Balliol College, Oxford, and under Lakshman Joo, later serving as Lecturer and then Professor at the University of Oxford (~1977–2015) and Fellow at All Souls College.

Alf Hiltebeitel specialized in Indology and religious studies. Educated at Haverford College and the University of Chicago Divinity School, he was a long-serving professor of religion at George Washington University from 1968, becoming Columbian Professor in 1981.
Alf Sommerfelt was a linguist who founded the Norwegian Association for Linguistics in 1924. He served as professor of linguistics at the University of Oslo from 1931 to 1962.

Alfons Fürst is a scholar of religious studies, history, and Indology who completed his promotion and habilitation at the University of Regensburg. He taught at Bamberg and became Professor of Ancient Church History at the University of Münster in 2000.

Alfonsa Ferrari was a scholar of Tibetology, Indology, and Buddhist studies. She studied under Giuseppe Tucci and Carlo Formichi at Sapienza University of Rome (~1937–1941), where she also conducted post-graduate research.

Alfred Bloom worked in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology. He earned his PhD at Harvard under Masatoshi Nagatomi and held faculty posts at the University of Oregon, the University of Hawaiʻi, and the Institute of Buddhist Studies.
Alfred Chilton Pearson was a scholar in linguistics and other fields. He was educated at Highgate School, King's College School, and Christ's College, Cambridge, where he studied under John Peile.

Alfred Cooper Woolner was a scholar of Indology and linguistics who studied at Trinity College, Oxford. He served as Principal of Oriental College (~1903–1936) and Vice Chancellor of the University of the Punjab (1928–1936).
